sections.h2: Where is the Putnam County recorder in Ottawa?
sections.html:
The Putnam County Recorder works from 245 E. Main Street in Ottawa, the same street address the county auditor lists. The recorder's resources page gives a phone of 419.523.6490, a toll-free line at 888.638.0042 and a fax at 419.523.4403.

Office hours run Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but recording hours end earlier, at 4:15 p.m. The contact page also lists the days the office closes: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Ottawa is the county seat. Wikipedia says the county was created in 1820, organized in 1834 and named for Israel Putnam, and that the Blanchard River, a key early transportation route, crosses it.

sections.h2: What is the order of steps to record a Putnam County deed?
sections.html:
Three stops come before the recorder sees a deed, and the county auditor's page spells them out. The order matters, because an unstamped deed is turned away.

  1. Take the legal description to the Tax Map Office, which sits in the engineer's office and answers at 419-523-6931. All legal descriptions must be pre-approved, and the document must meet the county's conveyance standards.
  2. Once the tax map staff sign the document, bring it to the auditor, who transfers it and collects the conveyance fee.
  3. Record the transferred deed with the recorder, who follows the standards and fees on its own site.

The auditor's office is at 245 East Main Street in Ottawa, phone 419-523-6686, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Its site includes a conveyance fee calculator under its Tools menu, so you can price the transfer before you go.

sections.h2: What does the Putnam County auditor charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html:
The auditor's real estate transfers page prints a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, and a transfer fee of 50 cents per parcel. The check must be for the exact amount of the conveyance fee, or the conveyance will not be processed.

Form DTE 100 goes with an ordinary sale. Form DTE 100 (EX) is used when the deed claims an exemption from the conveyance fee. The county's forms page carries both, so you can fill them in ahead of the visit.

Ohio also lets a county commission adopt a transfer tax of up to 30 cents per hundred dollars of value under R.C. 322.02, paid by the grantor to the auditor before the deed goes to the recorder. If you are unsure whether it applies, ask the auditor, since the conveyance calculator is the quickest check of the total.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost in Putnam County?
sections.html:
The recorder's FAQ points to a fee page and says the office charges a $4.00 fee for each marginal notation. The base amounts come from the statute, R.C. 317.32.

  • First two pages: $17 base fee and $17 housing trust fund fee.
  • Each later page: $4 base and $4 housing trust fund.
  • A preservation surcharge of up to $5 per instrument, kept by the county general fund.
  • Certified copy: $1 base and $1 trust fund per page.

The county adds $20 for a document that fails its document standards. Those standards, set under R.C. 317.114, require at least a 10-point font, black or blue ink only, no highlighting, paper between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches, a 3-inch top margin on page one, a 1.5-inch top margin on later pages and 1 inch on each side and the bottom. Court papers, plats, DD 214 discharges, state and federal documents and instruments signed before July 1, 2009 are exempt.

sections.h2: Which Putnam County offices matter in a home sale?
sections.html:
The table sets out what each office prints for the public, drawn from the county's own sites.

Putnam County offices a seller visits, with figures as published on the recorder and auditor sites
OfficeStep in a salePublished detail
Tax Map OfficePre-approves the legal description419-523-6931, located in the engineer's office
AuditorTransfers the deed, collects the conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 plus $.50 per parcel; 419-523-6686

The auditor's home page also posts a delinquent real estate list and counts 29,689 parcels as of 2023. A list like that is worth a look if you are selling a house that may have fallen behind on tax.

sections.h2: How can I record a Putnam County deed electronically or by mail?
sections.html:
The recorder's e-recording page says the service now covers deeds and other transfer documents, and names three approved vendors: Simplifile at 1.800.460.5657, CSC at 1.866.652.0111 and Erecording Partners at 1.888.325.3365. You work through one of them rather than the county directly.

The FAQ describes how fast things move. Documents recorded at the counter go back immediately, documents e-recorded are returned immediately, and documents delivered by mail are sent out the next business day. The office also requires a full legal description, including on releases and assignments, and maintains tract indexing by geography.

Records search is online. The FAQ says the indexes are open to everyone, viewing images needs a free online subscriber form, and documents are indexed on the computer starting January 1, 1993. A recording notification service is also offered.

sections.h2: What tools does the Putnam County auditor's site offer sellers?
sections.html:
The auditor's home page describes a Tools menu with sales reports, delinquency reports, the conveyance calculator and a tax estimator. A GIS parcel viewer sits behind the Map link, and an Info section holds the forms the state and the office provide.

The same page posts the 2025 delinquent parcels list. Search your parcel before you list, then call the auditor at 419-523-6686 if the record looks wrong.

sections.h2: What else does the Putnam County recorder do?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office runs the county's Ohio Century Farm registrations. A farm qualifies after 100 years in one family, and the recorder will meet with a family to check eligibility. It also keeps military discharge records, which are the DD 214 files veterans need for benefits.

Putnam County is mostly rural. Wikipedia reports 84.2% of residents in rural areas in the 2020 census and 83.8% of occupied homes owner-occupied, in a county of 484 square miles and 34,451 people. The county board of education operates nine school districts.

For a seller with a farm, a probated home or a house with an unpaid balance, the paperwork above still applies. A cash buyer can take the property as it is and pay these fees from the sale at closing.

faqs.q: What are the Putnam County recorder's hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and recording hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. It closes on the observed holidays the recorder's contact page lists.

faqs.q: What does the Putnam County auditor charge for a deed transfer?
faqs.a: The auditor prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, plus 50 cents per parcel. The check must match the conveyance fee exactly.

faqs.q: Do I need approval before I bring a deed to the Putnam County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The legal description must be pre-approved by the Tax Map Office, which is in the engineer's office, and the auditor must transfer the deed before it is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's page says e-recording now includes deeds and transfer documents, and lists Simplifile, CSC and Erecording Partners as approved vendors.

faqs.q: How much is a marginal notation in Putnam County?
faqs.a: The recorder's FAQ says $4.00 for each marginal notation. A nonconforming document costs an extra $20.00 on top of the recording fee.
